title: Thresholded failsafe decision graph for region/tier routing and auto-fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a decision-graph based failsafe for automatic fallback triggers across region selection, tier routing, and model-variant fallbacks. The goal is to unify multi-signal inputs (429s, per-second timeouts, error-rate spikes, queueing latency, and tenant-weighted priorities) into an explainable score that drives soft-open circuit breakers, staged evictions of model variants, and route-level probed failovers. This reduces customer-visible errors during overloads while preserving throughput and unit cost targets.
acceptance_criteria: Decision graph produces a single normalized score per route in < 10ms median time
Soft-open circuit breaker transitions implemented: CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN -> HARD_OPEN with configurable hysteresis
Per-tenant gravity + decay applied so transient spikes do not permanently blacklist a tenant
Canary probe mechanism validates fallback variant health within configured probe budget (default 0.5% of traffic)
Integration tests for 429-driven and timeout-driven failovers cover expected state transitions
Dashboard shows score decomposition (429_contrib, timeout_contrib, err_rate_contrib, latency_contrib) and historical transitions
implementation_notes: Score construction: weighted sum of normalized signals with tunable weights by tier/region: score = w1*exp(429_rate/scale1) + w2*(p50_latency/lat_scale) + w3*err_rate + w4*timeout_rate
Hysteresis: use separate open/close thresholds with momentum windows (open threshold 0.8, close threshold 0.45, window 30s) to avoid flapping
Soft-open behavior: when score crosses soft-open threshold, mark route as degraded and route X% of traffic to fallback variant + continue probes to primary; escalate to hard-open if score persists
Per-tenant probation logic: apply decay half-life to per-tenant score so older spikes fade. Default decay = 120s half-life; configurable per-account
Regional weighting: add cost penalty term to score when routing to expensive regions; favor local-region fallback before cross-region evacuation
Variant eviction policy: ordered by quality score (latency/cost/accuracy). Eviction removes lowest-ranked compatible variants first, preserving a minimum of one fallback variant
Probe design: lightweight text-only requests that exercise model warming and KV cache; probes run from the same cell ideally, and results feed back into score as a health multiplier
Telemetry hooks: emit score, contributing signals, breaker_state, evicted_variants, probe_results; tag by route, region, tier, tenant
Performance: prioritize in-memory computation and incremental updates; avoid heavy DB calls in hot path. Keep scoring code < 1000ns per request where possible
Config surface: route policy config includes thresholds, weights, per-tenant overrides, probe budget, and fallback variant ordering
testing_plan: Unit tests for score normalization and threshold hysteresis
Integration test: synthetic 429 storm causing soft-open then hard-open transitions within expected time windows
Chaos test: simulate regional network partition and verify graceful reroute to fallback variants and preserved SLOs
Perf test: ensure scoring adds < 1% p95 latency to end-to-end path under typical load (1k rps route)
Canary rollout: start with 1% of routes behind feature flag, monitor metrics for 24h before wider enablement
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: dev env -> internal staging with canary probes -> 1% customer traffic for 48h -> 10% for 7d -> 100% with automatic rollback if error-rate or customer-impact thresholds exceeded.

2026-02-24 Marco Gonzalez: Spike prototype implemented a simple weighted score and a soft-open flag. Observed correct state transitions in local sim. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123
2026-02-28 Lina Wu (SRE): Requested addition of per-tenant decay to avoid noisy neighbor blacklisting. Also asked for explicit probe budget to avoid probe amplification during outages.
2026-03-03 Product (Daniel Kim): Confirmed target UX for Console: show score decomposition and allow manual override of fallback order per route. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-06 Perf (TJ Morgan): Microbench results: scoring median 650ns on c6g-like CPU when implemented in C++; JS path currently 2.4us. Plan: implement hot path in runtime native module.
2026-03-09 Security (Priya Reddy): Quick review - probes must not expose customer data. Confirmed probes use synthetic payloads and sanitized telemetry. No additional KMS changes required.
2026-03-12 Marco Gonzalez: Merged initial scoring + soft-open state machine behind feature flag. Deploying to staging. Next: integrate variant eviction ordering and dashboard telemetry.
